findings.issue: 見とく = 見て+おく ('watch it / get the watching done in advance'), not 'leave the TV on' (that would be つけておく). The literal gloss changes the verb's action from watching to leaving powered on, contradicting en/pt and the token glosses.
findings.current: I'll leave the TV on, okay.
findings.suggested: TV, (I'll) watch (and have it done in advance), okay.

findings.issue: 終わる is non-past ('is ending / will end'), but 'March is over.' asserts a completed state (三月が終わった). It also contradicts the record's own expl_en, which says 'the month of March is coming to an end'.
findings.suggested: March is coming to an end.

findings.issue: 会場 means venue/hall (local do evento), not palco (= 舞台/ステージ). 'Saiu ao palco' over-specifies; the record's own lit_pt and token gloss correctly say 'local do evento'.
findings.current: Ele saiu ao palco representando a turma.
findings.suggested: Ele foi ao local do evento representando a turma.

findings.issue: 会場 means venue/hall, not stage; 'went out on stage' adds a referent not in the Japanese. The record's own lit_en and token gloss correctly say 'venue'.
findings.current: He went out on stage representing the class.
findings.suggested: He went out to the venue representing the class.

findings.issue: 'As lately as yesterday' is unidiomatic English ('lately' cannot be used in the as...as construction); the natural rendering of 来たばかり + きのう is 'only (just) yesterday'.
findings.current: He came as lately as yesterday.
